newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Central America to propose trade pact to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Central America to propose trade pact to Clinton.

text.p: Central American leaders plan to propose a free trade agreement with the United States when they meet President Bill Clinton in May, Honduras's foreign minister said on Wednesday.
"We're going to propose to the United States a free trade treaty, naturally giving Central America some tariff preferences," Foreign Minister Delmer Panting told reporters.

He said the region's leaders would present the proposal first to U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright at a meeting in Washington next Tuesday. It would be brought up again when they meet Clinton in San Jose, Costa Rica, around May 9th or 10th.

He said the countries -- Guatemala, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Costa Rica, Panama and Honduras -- were seeking to recapture some of the trade ground lost when Mexico joined the North American Free Trade Agreement with the United States and Canada in 1994, giving Mexico preferential tariffs for its exports.

On Tuesday, Costa Rican Foreign Minister Fernando Naranjo said the region would seek free trade with the United States before the year 2005, when governments across the continent have pledged to set up a hemisphere-wide free-trade zone.

But he said procuring U.S. investment in Central America would be the top priority during the Clinton visit. It will be the first time the U.S. leader has visited the region, which was torn by guerrilla wars in three countries in the 1980s but is now embarked on an era of free-market ecomic reform during peacetime.
